name: Reservoir rUSD
oneLiner: rUSD is Reservoir's mintable dollar stablecoin, redeemable 1:1 for USDC, USDT, or USD1 and backed by a mixed RWA and digital-asset balance sheet.
collateral: Reservoir protocol balance sheet of stablecoin PSM liquidity, RWA allocations, DeFi lending markets, and governance-approved credit strategies monitored through Reservoir's live reserve endpoint
pegMechanism: Users can mint and redeem rUSD 1:1 against USDC, USDT, or USD1 through Reservoir's Peg Stability Module, while Credit Enforcer contracts constrain liquidity, solvency, and capital ratios before protocol asset reallocations.

applicabilityBasis.summary: rUSD is a USD-pegged, 1:1 mintable/redeemable stablecoin that structurally meets the GENIUS Act definition of a payment stablecoin. However, the issuer explicitly excludes US persons from the protocol and interface via its Terms of Service, and the ToS is governed by Cayman Islands law, indicating the issuer has not sought any US regulatory pathway.

genius.notes: The Reservoir Terms of Service explicitly state that rUSD is not offered to US persons and that US persons are not permitted to use the Interface or Protocol. The ToS is governed by Cayman Islands law. No named legal issuer entity is disclosed; the protocol is operated by Reservoir Protocol, incubated by Fortunafi. No GENIUS Act pathway, PPSI application, or foreign exception engagement was identified.

blacklistabilityReview.evidence: A freeze/blacklist capability exists now on rUSD's live Tempo deployment: rUSD on Tempo is a TIP-20 protocol precompile at 0x20c0000000000000000000007f7ba549dd0251b9, and the TIP-20 standard ships every token with pause(), TIP-403 whitelist/blacklist transfer policies, and burnBlocked(). The token's DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE is actively held by Reservoir operations EOA 0xb7570e32ded63b25163369d5eb4d8e89e70e5602 (granted at creation via TIP20Factory, Tempo block 12113547), which can at any time activate a blacklist policy, pause all transfers, or burn blocked balances; at Tempo block 32485354 the token reads paused() = false and transferPolicyId() = 1 (always-allow), but the control surface is live. By contrast the canonical Ethereum token 0x09d4214c03d01f49544c0448dbe3a27f768f2b34 (verified Blockscout source 'Stablecoin', non-proxy, OpenZeppelin AccessControl + ERC20Burnable only) has no blacklist, pause, freeze, or arbitrary-burn path — its sole privileged function is MINTER-role mint — and every EVM sidechain deployment is verified vanilla LayerZero OFT v2 + Ownable with no freeze surface (Arbitrum RusdOft source re-verified 2026-07-30), while the Solana mint has freezeAuthority unset. The canonical supply therefore carries no freeze reach, but the tracked Tempo TIP-20 deployment carries a real admin-controlled freeze/blacklist surface, making the honest asset-level answer true.

mintAuthority.summary: rUSD issuance runs through Reservoir PSMs and the Credit Enforcer. Both the PSM and Credit Enforcer share the same DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE holder: Reservoir EOA 0xb7570e32.

controls.capDescription: Credit Enforcer enforces solvency, debt limits, and operational constraints on PSM minting.
controls.evidence: At Ethereum block 25295029, hasRole(DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE, 0xb7570e32) on the Credit Enforcer returned True. RoleGranted logs confirm deployer (0x6ed13690) revoked and 0xb7570e32 is current admin.

sources.label: Reservoir Credit Enforcer RoleGranted events at Ethereum block 25295029

controls.evidence: At Ethereum block 25295029, eth_getCode returned 0x (EOA). hasRole(DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE, this) = True on both PSM and Credit Enforcer. Deployer EOA 0x6ed13690 revoked at blocks 20564175/20564179.

review.evidence: At Ethereum block 25295029: PSM and Credit Enforcer DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE confirmed as EOA 0xb7570e32 via hasRole() and RoleGranted/RoleRevoked log scan on Blockscout. Both contracts are non-proxy AccessControl deployments. All mint-capable surfaces confirmed. Re-verified at Ethereum block 25575157 on 2026-07-20: the Reservoir USDC Peg Stability Module 0x4809010926aec940b550D34a46A52739f996D75D and the Credit Enforcer 0x04716DB62C085D9e08050fcF6F7D775A03d07720 both still return hasRole(DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE, 0xb7570e32ded63b25163369d5eb4d8e89e70e5602) = true, both still read a zero EIP-1967 implementation slot confirming they are non-proxy deployments, and eth_getCode on the admin is still empty, confirming a codeless externally owned account. Economic-control adjudication: a single unprotected EOA administers both the PSM and the Credit Enforcer that sets the issuance ceiling, with no multisig, timelock, or independent bound, so the mint cap is economically unbounded. Reservoir publishes a real-time reserves view rather than a periodic report, so reconciliation cadence is continuous (the self attestor tier is already recorded separately under proofOfReserves), and no financial regulator supervises Reservoir.

Reservoir's official contract registry lists 'rUSD OFT adapter' 0xc593478d188259eaf3706b070fb8c17cf00b25b8 and 'rUSD TIP20' 0x20c0000000000000000000007f7ba549dd0251b9 on Tempo, resolving this route as Reservoir's own LayerZero wiring (DefiLlama's old 'Stargate Hydra' label no longer appears in its current reservoir-stablecoin config, and Stargate Hydra only wraps USDC/USDT/WETH). At Tempo block 32485354: the TIP-20 preinstall (1-byte precompile code, name 'Reservoir Stablecoin', 6 decimals, totalSupply 10 raw units of dust) granted DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE at creation to Reservoir operations EOA 0xb7570e32ded63b25163369d5eb4d8e89e70e5602 (block 12113547) and ISSUER_ROLE to the OFT adapter (block 16478140, granted by 0xb7570e32); the adapter returns token() = the TIP-20 and endpoint() = 0x20bb7c2e2f4e5ca2b4c57060d1ae2615245dcc9c (eid 30410) whose delegates(adapter) = 0xb7570e32, and the adapter's proxy admin 0xbccbc2a5cdef7d85184c97284ccea0a3de9b05db has owner() = 0x0, locking the implementation. On Ethereum at block 25689424 the canonical rUSD OFT adapter 0xf0e9f6d9ba5d1b3f76e0f82f9dcdb9ebeef4b4da returns token() = native rUSD and peers(30410) = the Tempo adapter, so rUSD mint/burn on Tempo runs only through LayerZero-verified messages between Reservoir's adapter pair (the Tempo-side peers(30101) entry is not yet set).

reserveReview.rationale: The Reservoir raw reserves API fetched on 2026-07-27 reported $35,590,265.61 of total assets across 10 rows (totalLiabilities $35,293,176.43, equity $297,089.18). Bucketing rows through the reviewed Reservoir adapter mapping yields: Hastra/Sentora PRIME 45.5% ($120,195.67 Hastra PRIME token + $16,073,753.70 Morpho Sentora PRIME), Pendle PT-USDat-27AUG2026 25.7% ($9,143,696.79), Aave GHO on Plasma/Monad 15.5% ($4,039,138.08 Plasma + $1,485,799.99 Monad), USDC 9.6% ($35,442.69 direct/PSM USDC + $3,392,592.23 Morpho Steakhouse Prime Instant V2), and the Agua Global Carry Vault 3.7% ($1,299,646.44); rounded slices sum to 100.0%. Since the 2026-07-20 review the USD1 bucket went to zero (no USD1 rows in the 2026-07-27 payload), so the 2.1% USD1 slice was removed, and the Agua vault slice grew from 2.6% to 3.7%. The Agua slice is no longer unmapped: at Ethereum block 25673162 (0x18703ca) the ERC-4626 at 0xa98b4a70e17e55045cde4972b95bc2e8cec22a0f returned asset() = USDC (0xa0b86991c6218b36c1d19d4a2e9eb0ce3606eb48), name 'Agua Global Carry Vault', symbol aguaUSDCgc, so the slice maps to its verified USDC underlying claim while the vault's undisclosed multi-strategy internals stay captured in its high risk tier and risk factors. Risk-tier judgment calls retained: PRIME stays high because it is Figure-originated HELOC private credit (per curator Sentora's own description) whose exit path is an unpublished Morpho market redemption; PT USDat stays high despite tokenized-treasury collateral because the position is a fixed-maturity Pendle principal token (matures 2026-08-27, 31 days out) carrying AMM-exit basis risk.

custodyProfile.reviewer: Kimi P2 reserve cohort rc-3 (lead usdd-tron-dao-reserve)
custodyProfile.uncertainty: Reservoir's balance sheet sits in protocol-controlled Asset Adapter and PSM contracts (the 2026-07-20 API rows resolve to adapter addresses 0x4809010926aec940b550d34a46a52739f996d75d, 0x3063C5907FAa10c01B242181Aa689bEb23D2BD65, 0x289C204B35859bFb924B9C0759A4FE80f610671c, and 0x8Cc5a546408C6cE3C9eeB99788F9EC3b8FA6b9F3), and neither the Terms of Service (2024-08-23) nor any docs.reservoir.xyz page reviewed today names a third-party custodian, trust, SPV, or holder claim on reserve assets, so no bankruptcy-remoteness structure is documented. Reserve re-use is the protocol's core yield model: docs state the balance sheet is allocated into RWA, lending markets, and DeFi strategies, and the ToS itself warns redemptions can lag when reserve assets must be sold or redeemed. Protocol admins (the PSM and Credit Enforcer DEFAULT_ADMIN is EOA 0xb7570e32 per the mint-authority review) can reallocate the balance sheet without holder consent. For the 44.8% PRIME sleeve, custody of the underlying Figure HELOC collateral sits upstream with Hastra/Democratized Prime and is not documented by Reservoir. No named legal issuer entity is disclosed (Cayman Islands governing law only), so holder recourse in an insolvency is untested; wallet-level segregation inside the adapter contracts is not disclosed.
